newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Macquarie says no buy-back plans.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Macquarie says no buy-back plans.

text.p: Macquarie Bank Ltd said on Monday it had no plans to return capital to shareholders or to make a takeover due to its high capital adequacy ratio (CAR).
Macquarie had a CAR of 13.6 percent at September 30 although this is lower than the 15.4 percent level at March 31.
This ratio compares with the Reserve Bank of Australia's minimum requirement of eight percent.

Chairman David Clarke said a high capital adequacy ratio was needed for investment bank activities. Asked by reporters if Macquarie planned either a takeover or share buy back, he replied: "We have no plans for either those two things."

"I think it is the nature of our business to have a capital adequacy ratio that is higher than the trading banks because we are very dependent on counter-party limits from other banks, they in turn are quite dependent on ratings...it is a healthy capital adequacy ratio and I think we can expect to be well and truely above the basic minimum," Clarke said.

Macquarie managing director Allan Moss said the fall in the capital adequacy ratio to current levels from the March 1996 level reflected a higher dividend payout ratio of 59 percent from 55 percent previously.
Macquarie reported a 21.1 percent increase in net profit to A$46.03 million for the six months ended September 30, 1996.
At 12.15 (0115 GMT), Macquarie shares were six cents lower at A$8.60.
